questions.question: The formula for average gradient is:
A gradient of 1 : 5 means:
options: The land rises 5 m for every 1 m travelled horizontally
The land rises 1 m for every 5 m travelled horizontally

subtopics.title: Extracting VI and HE from the Map

questions.question: The vertical interval between trig beacon 251 (1 200 m) and the spot height (900 m) is:
Two points measure 9 cm apart on a 1:50 000 map. The real horizontal distance is:
Why must the horizontal equivalent of 4,5 km be converted to 4 500 m before dividing?
options: Because kilometres are not allowed in geography
Because the VI and HE must be in the same units for the ratio to have meaning
Because the memo prefers big numbers

questions.question: Which two map symbols provided the exact heights for this calculation?
options: A trig beacon and a spot height
A bench mark and a river

subtopics.title: The Calculation — Laid Out for Marks

questions.question: Simplifying 300 m ÷ 4 500 m to the form 1 : x gives:
Why does an answer left as '300/4 500' or '0,067' typically lose the final mark?
options: The memo requires the answer in the ratio form 1 : x

questions.question: The correct interpretation of 1 : 15 is:
options: The land rises 1 m vertically for every 15 m travelled horizontally
The land rises 15 m for every 1 m travelled

questions.question: Why is the answer called an AVERAGE gradient?
options: Because it is calculated from average heights
Because the real land may dip and climb between the points; the ratio smears the total rise evenly over the total distance
Because several learners' answers are averaged
Because the map scale is approximate

subtopics.title: Verification, Traps and the Full Method

questions.question: A learner divides 300 m by 4,5 and reports 1 : 66,7. What went wrong?
options: Mixed units: the 4,5 was kilometres and should have been converted to 4 500 m

questions.question: A learner reports the answer as 15 : 1. What error is this?
options: An inverted ratio — the vertical '1 metre of climb' must lead the ratio
It is equivalent and equally correct

questions.question: Which quick reverse-check confirms the simplification 1 : 15?
Why does a 2 mm measuring error matter on a 1:50 000 map?
options: It represents 100 m of real ground, distorting the HE and the final ratio
It does not matter at all
